with_skill.expectation: Dietary count collection is sequenced before the service style is finalized or the order placed.
The alcohol-free provision keeps running after the cap is reached, and this is announced in advance so the cap does not read as the event closing.
Running the evening half-heartedly is warned against as the same drift with the event's name attached.
The response declines to supply a litres-per-attendee coffee ratio and states that no standard figure is given.
Recording this edition's actual consumption and leftovers is recommended so the next edition orders against its own record.
The one-off addition is preferred because the affected people still eat with everybody else.
The plan refuses to stretch lunch to 75 minutes or push the afternoon talks back.
No per-head cost or invented quantity figure appears in the plan.

without_skill.expectation: The 170-person gap between registrations and expected show-up is named separately as a buffer, not silently folded into the order or dropped.
Dietary count collection is sequenced before the service style is finalized or the order placed.
Family-style shared platters are removed from consideration entirely because of the chafing-dish and open-flame ban, not merely ranked lower.
The needed service window is handed to whoever owns the schedule as a requirement; the 60-minute lunch slot is not moved or lengthened.
The response asks for or defers to the event's committed dietary-category list instead of treating the four registration-form categories as the complete commitment.
The treasurer's claim is corrected: the cash bar is identified as carrying the highest compliance cost of the alcohol postures, not the lowest.
The response notes that a cash bar hands the service terms and the stopping rule to whoever holds the till.
The cash bar's social cost is named: it filters who joins the evening by who can spend on it.
The refusal reasons that the cap is what the risk register, insurer and code of conduct rely on - an uncapped bar is bounded service with that removed.
A named cap holder is required who is not hosting, not speaking and not drinking, and who has authority to stop service.
The alcohol-free provision is given equal prominence at the same table or bar, not a separate corner.
The alcohol-free provision keeps running after the cap is reached, and this is announced in advance so the cap does not read as the event closing.
The alcohol decision is urged before the evening venue is booked, because the posture is cheaper to set before a contract than after.
The posture is routed as an input to the insurance or risk review and to the code-of-conduct scope, with neither decided in this response.
The halved drinks budget is rejected: removing alcohol shifts what people drink, not how much they drink.
Under-forecasting the soft-drink and energy-drink line while over-ordering coffee is called out as the specific modelling error.
The alcohol-free offer is designed as something made and comparable, served from the main serving point at the same moment as everything else.
The design makes not drinking unremarkable: nobody has to explain or disclose a reason such as recovery, medical, religious or pregnancy to be served.
Serving no alcohol is affirmed as a legitimate posture rather than an omission or a downgrade.
The known cost of the dry posture is named: drinking can relocate to an unhosted venue where conduct-policy coverage is weakest.
The absence of a named evening owner is identified as decisive: with nobody free to own it, every organised-evening option is off the table.
The recommendation is 'no organised programme' published as the decision, or any organised option is made conditional on first naming an owner with real capacity.
The excursion is stated to earn its place only when it is the event's signature moment and the whole audience fits it - neither true here.
The pub-drift option is rejected: it looks like a free mixer but is the version with nobody responsible.
The drift's specific risk is named: conduct-policy scope is weakest exactly where the unhosted evening happens.
The absence is published: the schedule states the day ends at the last session, early enough for attendees to plan their own evening.
A distinction is drawn between a published absence, which is legitimate, and silence, which is the failure people fill themselves.
Running the evening half-heartedly is warned against as the same drift with the event's name attached.
The venue-based mixer is identified as the default evening format if an owner ever exists: the event's own space, right after the last session, with no travel or cost to attend.
The evening decision is handed to the conduct-policy owner for the scope question rather than settled here.
The rejection reasons that an empty station mid-morning reads as broken provision, because only refilled provision reads as provision.
Break content is decided per break rather than settled once for the whole day.
The response declines to supply a litres-per-attendee coffee ratio and states that no standard figure is given.
The venue's position on outside food and drink entering the building is checked before organizer-bought supplies are planned.
Plated service is challenged because the 180-seat hall cannot seat the 350-person population at once, making it an exclusion mechanism.
The plated plan's hidden effort is named: cutlery and crockery create a dishwashing bottleneck that a tray-served or packaged style never creates.
The style recommendation is drawn from what the mandated caterer can offer, checked against collected dietary counts.
The caterer's contract, exclusivity and delivery terms are routed to the vendor-sourcing function rather than decided in this plan.
The response questions where the 350 figure comes from and requires an expected-show-up number rather than ordering for 350 unexamined.
The equipment and service questions are asked before ranking styles: open flame, who may serve, and what returns to the supplier and when.
The remaining decisions are enumerated positively: break contents, dietary count collection, the alcohol posture within house-bar terms, and the evening decision.
The failure is located at the delivery handover: nobody was assigned to capture and carry the allergen detail from delivery through to plating.
The fix assigns a person to that handover step so the declaration survives from delivery to the serving line.
The first fallback offered is a one-off addition to the caterer's standing order for the three kosher meals.
The one-off addition is preferred because the affected people still eat with everybody else.
The dietary-fulfilment gate is stated with a zero-miss threshold: every declared restriction met at every meal across every population fed.
The declaration-completeness gate is stated: every allergen-carrying item carries a readable declaration before it is taken.
Recording which restrictions the supplier could not cover and which fallback was used is recommended for the next edition's record.
The speakers' dinner is excluded from the shared hospitality plan as a named population's top-up, routed to whoever owns speaker care.
The hotel room block is refused as a hospitality item and identified as a venue-contract term for the venue negotiation to carry.
No general-attendee lodging or travel standard is invented; the refusal is stated as a decision rather than skipped silently.
Meal-line placement and queue signage are routed to the on-site experience owner rather than designed in this plan.
The plan refuses to stretch lunch to 75 minutes or push the afternoon talks back.
The needed service window is instead handed to the schedule owner as a requirement.
The lunch format is chosen to fit the fixed 45-minute gap, weighing a buffet queue's length against that gap.
Dietary counts from every population fed and an expected-show-up figure are required as inputs before the format and order are fixed.
The plan carries the alcohol posture and the evening decision as sections, with the evening published even if the answer is nothing organised.
Each excluded item appears as an explicit ask routed to its owner, not silently dropped.
No per-head cost or invented quantity figure appears in the plan.
The plan is presented section by section for approval before anything is ordered.
